title: Add “activation recipe” example app (chat + tracing + cost breakdown)
author: Jada Williams
body:
## Summary
Adds a new “activation recipe” example app intended to get a self-serve developer to a production-like first success quickly, while also showcasing (a) streaming chat, (b) tracing hooks, and (c) a simple cost/latency breakdown view.

This is the example referenced by the retargeting landing page variant and the onboarding “Next step” email CTA.

## Why
We keep hearing that the quickstart gets users to a 2xx, but doesn’t clearly demonstrate what “good” looks like in production: streaming, request IDs/traces, and basic unit economics. This example app packages those into a single runnable project with copy-paste env vars and a simple UI.

## What’s included
- Streaming chat UI (SSE) with a minimal “system prompt + user messages” flow
- Request-level tracing:
  - Adds a `x-redwood-request-id` header on every request
  - Propagates `traceparent` when present (optional)
  - Displays request id in the UI and logs it to the server console
- Cost + latency breakdown panel:
  - Displays tokens in/out + total tokens (from response usage)
  - Estimates cost using a lightweight price table (documented as a sample; not a billing source of truth)
  - Shows time-to-first-token and total duration
- Troubleshooting section + “common errors” mapping (401/403, model not found, streaming disconnect)

## App structure
- `examples/activation-recipe/`
  - `apps/web` (Next.js) UI
  - `apps/api` (Next.js route handlers) proxying requests to Redwood API
  - `packages/shared` small helpers for headers, usage parsing, and price table

## Setup
1) `cd examples/activation-recipe`
2) `cp .env.example .env.local`
3) Set:
   - `REDWOOD_API_KEY=...`
   - `REDWOOD_BASE_URL=https://api.redwoodinference.com` (or your private endpoint)
   - `REDWOOD_MODEL=redwood/verified-chat` (default in example)
4) `pnpm install && pnpm dev`

## Notes / guardrails
- The cost calculator is intentionally labeled “estimate” and uses a static table to avoid implying billing accuracy.
- The example uses the standard SDK-compatible request format and should work across Hosted/Dedicated/Private endpoints.
- No product analytics events added here (this repo is examples-only); attribution is handled on the landing page + console side.

## Screenshots
- Chat + streaming + request id: included in README as a GIF
- Cost/latency panel: included in README as a screenshot

## Checklist
- [x] Runs end-to-end with a fresh key
- [x] Streaming works behind a typical corporate proxy (basic retry)
- [x] Lint + typecheck pass
- [x] README includes a “copy/paste curl” fallback

## Follow-ups (not in this PR)
- Add a Python variant (separate repo / directory)
- Replace static price table with an optional call to a public pricing endpoint once available
commits: feat(chat): streaming UI + server proxy route
feat(tracing): propagate trace headers + show request id
docs: add README, screenshots, troubleshooting, and curl fallback
chore: align lint/tsconfig with repo defaults
conversation:
Tyler Benson (review): This is great for the retargeting flow. Can we make sure the README doesn’t over-claim “cost” accuracy? Also, the landing page will deep link to a section anchor—please add stable headings.

Jada Williams (author): Good call. Updated language to “estimate” in UI + README, added a disclaimer, and made headings stable (## Run locally, ## Troubleshooting, ## Cost & latency).

Marissa Cole (review): Can we include a link to the Console’s latency/cost dashboards as the “next step” after running? Also: would love streaming to be the default path.

Jada Williams (author): Added “Next steps in Console” section with links and made streaming the default (with a non-streaming curl fallback).

Paula Mendes (review): For tracing—do we want `traceparent` pass-through AND a request id? Support will likely ask for request id. Also ensure we’re not logging keys.

Jada Williams (author): Kept both. Request id is generated server-side and shown in UI; only logs request id + timings. No auth headers logged.

Kenji Nakamura (review): Minor UX: the cost panel should show time-to-first-token (TTFT) separately from total time; that’s the benchmark story we tell.

Jada Williams (author): Added TTFT measurement on the client and displayed it in CostPanel.

CI note: First run failed on lint (unused import + React hook deps). Fixed in 5f2a9c1 and re-ran.

Approvals:
- Marissa Cole: Approved
- Paula Mendes: Approved
- Tyler Benson: Approved
- Kenji Nakamura: Approved

Merged via squash after approvals.
release_notes: New example: `examples/activation-recipe` — streaming chat app demonstrating tracing + basic cost/latency breakdown for onboarding/retargeting flows.
